metaDescription: Compare key competitors and substitutes on features, pricing, messaging, and positioning — structured for differentiation. Newon COMPETITOR ANALYSIS.
headline:
Don't list competitors —
make them comparable.
lead: We compare key competitors and substitutes across positioning, features, pricing, messaging, and target. Product pages, reviews, pricing, and IR material are organized into a Competitor Matrix and summary your team can use in differentiation and strategy conversations.
overviewTitle:
You know the names.
Not the comparison criteria.
overviewBody: Competitor names come up often in product, marketing, and investment conversations. But comparing features, pricing, messaging, and target on the same criteria is harder.
Each company's site, product pages, pricing, reviews, app stores, and IR offer different angles — but rarely in a structure teams can use immediately.
COMPETITOR ANALYSIS starts by defining who to compare and on what axes. Then we collect and organize material into a Competitor Matrix, positioning summary, and gap analysis in one deliverable.

faqs.q: How many competitors can you compare?
faqs.a: We define set size by goal and source access. Typically 3–10 players — we confirm fit before starting.
Features, pricing, packaging, messaging, target, channels, and more — axes matched to your goal. We agree criteria before starting.
Document and table-first: Competitor Matrix, positioning summary, gap analysis. Presentation summaries can be included.

faqs.q: How is this different from MARKET RESEARCH?
faqs.a: COMPETITOR ANALYSIS focuses on competitor and substitute comparison. If overall market structure is the need, MARKET RESEARCH may fit better — scopes can be linked.

faqs.q: Can our product be included in the matrix?
faqs.a: Yes, when you want. Share internal material and we can include a 'You' column.

faqs.q: Can this connect to BUILD or MVP?
faqs.a: Yes. Comparison can feed feature priority, positioning, and go-to-market decisions.
We work within agreed scope only. An NDA can be signed when required.
